words.gloss: udāvarta (reversed, upward course of Vāta; standard)

words.gram: n. inst. sg. used as ind.

hindi: उदावर्त यानी वात का उलटा ऊपर की ओर चलना, यदि उपेक्षित हो, तो अचानक गर्भ सहित गर्भवती स्त्री को नष्ट कर दे।
english: Udāvarta (a disorder in which Vāta runs upward in reverse), if neglected, would suddenly destroy the pregnant woman together with her fetus.
notes: Printed udāvartto (rtt) is the book-wide orthographic normalisation. atipātayet = literally 'would cause to fall away'; 'destroy' is the plain sense; 'cause to miscarry' is a possible narrower reading, since the object is the woman together with her fetus. Hindi uses वात for the doṣa. Modern equivalent (probable): udāvarta = reversal of the downward course of Vāta with retention of stool and wind, roughly an obstructive bowel disorder (constipation or ileus type).

words.gloss: sexual intercourse (vyavāya; standard); and the like
fetus; bed (garbhaśayyā, probably the womb; probable)
liver (yakṛt; standard); spleen (plīha; standard); intestines (antra; standard); gaps

words.gram: pres. mid. part. ava-√lamb, m. nom. sg.

hindi: जिस स्त्री का गर्भ, फिर दोषों के अत्यधिक संचय से, या कहे हुए व्यवाय यानी मैथुन आदि से, या अन्य रोगों से, या माता और सन्तान के पहले संचित कर्म से, बन्धन से छूट जाता है, जैसे फल डंठल से; वह बन्धन से छूटा हुआ गर्भ गर्भशय्या यानी सम्भवतः गर्भाशय को लाँघकर यकृत्, प्लीहा यानी तिल्ली और आँतों के छिद्रों में लटकता हुआ कोष्ठ में क्षोभ उत्पन्न करता है।
english: Of her whose fetus (garbha) is released from its bond, whether by an excessive accumulation of doṣas, or by those stated, vyavāya (sexual intercourse) and the like, or by other diseases, or by the earlier accumulated action of the mother and of the offspring, like a fruit from its stalk: that fetus, with its bond released, having passed beyond the bed of the fetus (garbhaśayyā, probably the womb), hanging in the gaps of the liver (yakṛt), spleen (plīha) and intestines (antra), brings about a disturbance of the koṣṭha (storehouse, belly).

text_flags.why: possible: the passive of √muc is mucyate; printed 'mocyate' (with o) may be a print slip, though a guṇa form could be an old variant

notes: One long sentence; the main clause begins at 'saḥ'. 'yathoktair vā vyavāyādibhir' is taken as 'or by those stated, vyavāya and the like'; the grammar could also join 'yathokta' with 'vyādhibhiḥ', so the scope of 'stated' is not firm. 'pūrvopacitena karmaṇā' = by earlier accumulated action (karman); the doctrinal sense is not expanded. garbhaśayyā = bed of the fetus, probably the womb (probable). The instrumental 'vivaraiḥ' with avalambamānaḥ is rendered loosely as 'in the gaps'. koṣṭha = storehouse, belly. The sentence is followed by 83, which continues the account. Genitive 'yasyāḥ' stands loosely with 'garbhaḥ' ('of whom the fetus'). Printed 'baṃdhanānmocyate' reads mocyate (guṇa vowel).
lines_deva: यस्याः पुनरतिमात्रदोषोपचयाद्यथोक्तैर्वा व्यवायादिभिरन्यैर्वा व्याधिभिः पूर्वोपचितेन वा जनन्यपत्ययोः कर्मणा बंधनान्मोच्यते गर्भः फलमिववृंतात् स मुक्तबंधनो गर्भशय्यामतिक्रम्य यकृत्प्लीहान्त्रविवरैर्वावलंबमानः कोष्ठसंक्षोभमापादयति
lines_iast: yasyāḥ punaratimātradoṣopacayādyathoktairvā vyavāyādibhiranyairvā vyādhibhiḥ pūrvopacitena vā jananyapatyayoḥ karmaṇā baṃdhanānmocyate garbhaḥ phalamivavṛṃtāt sa muktabaṃdhano garbhaśayyāmatikramya yakṛtplīhāntravivarairvāvalaṃbamānaḥ koṣṭhasaṃkṣobhamāpādayati

words.gloss: flank (kukṣi); bladder (basti; probable); sides; belly; yoni; pain; distension (ānāha); stool; urine; retentions

hindi: तब कोष्ठ के क्षोभ से अपान वायु बार-बार कुक्षि, बस्ति यानी सम्भवतः मूत्राशय, पार्श्व, उदर और योनि में पीड़ा, आनाह यानी पेट फूलना, तथा मल और मूत्र का रुकना उत्पन्न करके कोमल गर्भ को रक्त के रूप में गिरा देती है।
english: Then, from the disturbance of the koṣṭha, the Apāna wind (vāyu), having repeatedly brought about pain in the flank (kukṣi), basti (probably the bladder), sides, belly and yoni, distension (ānāha), and retentions of stool and urine, causes the young fetus to fall away in the form of blood.
notes: Compound 'kukṣi...yoni-śūla-ānāha-viṇ-mūtra-saṅgān' is read as: pain in kukṣi, basti, sides, belly and yoni; ānāha; retention of stool and of urine (the scope of 'śūla' over the five places is a reading, not certain). basti = bladder is probable (basti also names the enema device). ānāha = distension of the belly with retention of stool and wind (standard). 'śoṇitabhāvena' = literally 'by the state of blood', taken as 'in the form of blood'. Continues 82 (GROUPING: appears to continue 82).
lines_deva: ततः कोष्ठसंक्षोभाद्वायुरपानो मुहुःकुक्षिबस्तिपार्श्वोदरयोनिशूलानाहविण्मूत्रसंगानापाद्य गर्भं च्यावयति तरुणं शोणितभावेन
lines_iast: tataḥ koṣṭhasaṃkṣobhādvāyurapāno muhuḥkukṣibastipārśvodarayoniśūlānāhaviṇmūtrasaṃgānāpādya garbhaṃ cyāvayati taruṇaṃ śoṇitabhāvena

hindi: वह पहले कहा जा चुका है।
english: That has been stated before.
notes: The referent of 'saḥ' (masculine) is not named in the unit; the text does not say what has been stated before (possibly the abortion, garbhasrāva, or the wind); not enriched. The printed so'bhihitaḥ = saḥ abhihitaḥ (regular sandhi). GROUPING: appears to continue 83.

hindi: पर गर्भ के बढ़ जाने पर पेट कठोर, स्थिर, ठण्डा और मानो भीतर पत्थर वाला दिखाई देता है।
english: But when the fetus (garbha) has grown, the belly (udara) appears stiff, still, cold, as if it had a stone inside.
notes: Printed 'garbhestabdhaṃ' joins garbhe and stabdham (spacing slip, no flag). The locative absolute 'vivṛddhe garbhe' is read as 'the fetus having grown'. stimita = still, motionless (it can also mean 'wet', not chosen). aśmagarbha = literally 'stone-interior'. The unit describes the belly in the case taken up in 86 (the dead fetus); the text does not say so here.

words.gloss: unclear (printed form; on a conjectural reading 'sink in')

words.gram: dvandva, n. acc. sg. used as ind.
n. abl. sg. used as ind.
tat-puruṣa, n. acc. sg. used as ind.

hindi: अत्यधिक पीड़ा होती है और गर्भ हिलता नहीं, अन्य प्रकट होते हैं, योनि से स्राव नहीं होता, और अनुमानित पाठ पर इसकी दोनों आँखें धँस जाती हैं; वैसे ही वह अरति यानी बेचैनी से अत्यन्त घिरी हुई कष्ट पाती है, अन्य प्रकार से चेष्टा करती है, निढाल होती है, थकती है, दिन-रात रोती है, सोती नहीं, प्रत्येक श्वास पर कठिनाई से साँस लेती है, अत्यन्त कष्ट से जीती है और क्षीण होती है; ऐसी स्त्री को मृतगर्भा यानी मरे गर्भ वाली जाने।
english: Pain arises in excess, and the fetus does not move; other (ones) appear; the yoni does not flow; and, on a conjectural reading, her two eyes sink in; likewise she, greatly beset by arati (restlessness), is distressed, acts differently, languishes, tires, weeps day and night, does not sleep, breathes with difficulty at each breath, lives (breathes) in great distress, and wastes away. One should know a woman of this kind to be mṛtagarbhā (one with a dead fetus).

text_flags.why: possible: 'saṃsyete' is not a known verb form; saṃsīdete (they sink in) or sraṃsete (they droop) would suit the dual subject akṣiṇī; the word is doubtful
possible: svapiti is the usual 3 sg. of √svap; 'svapniti' looks like a print slip (n inserted)

notes: The verb 'saṃsyete' is not a known form: a dual verb is needed for the dual subject 'akṣiṇī' (two eyes); saṃ-sad (saṃsīdete, 'sink in') is a conjecture only, so the translation says 'on a conjectural reading'. 'anyāni' = other (signs), the noun is not stated and is shown as '(ones)'. 'yoniḥ' is taken as the subject of 'na sravati' (no flow from the yoni). 'pratyucchvāsāt kṛcchrāt' is rendered 'at each breath, with difficulty' (ablatives used loosely). 'svapniti' is printed; the standard form is svapiti. 'kṣayati' = wastes away is probable (√kṣi, dwindle); 'prāṇiti' = breathes/lives. tāmyati/śrāmyati: languishes/tires (exact shade of tāmyati is not firm). 'arati' = restlessness, discontent. The closing 'iti' follows 'kṣayati' (end of the list of signs). Dead-fetus signs as printed are translated without comment on modern medicine. Other conjectural repairs for saṃsyete (all unproven): saṃśīyete (they shrink; s/ś confusion) or saṃsyandete (they flow). The verb stays unclear. Modern equivalent (probable): mṛtagarbhā = woman carrying a dead fetus (intrauterine fetal death).
lines_deva: शूलमधिकमुपजायते न च स्पंदते गर्भोऽन्यानि प्रादुर्भवंति न स्रवति योनिरक्षिणीचास्याः संस्येते तथा भृशमरतिपरीता व्यथतेऽन्यथा चेष्टते ताम्यतिश्राम्यति रोदित्यहर्निशं न स्वप्निति प्रत्युच्छ्वासात्कृच्छ्राच्छ्वसित्यतिकष्टं प्राणिति क्षयतीत्येवंविधां स्त्रियं मृतगर्भां विद्यान्
lines_iast: śūlamadhikamupajāyate na ca spaṃdate garbho'nyāni prādurbhavaṃti na sravati yonirakṣiṇīcāsyāḥ saṃsyete tathā bhṛśamaratiparītā vyathate'nyathā ceṣṭate tāmyatiśrāmyati rodityaharniśaṃ na svapniti pratyucchvāsātkṛcchrācchvasityatikaṣṭaṃ prāṇiti kṣayatītyevaṃvidhāṃ striyaṃ mṛtagarbhāṃ vidyān

hindi: उस गर्भ को, जो कभी-कभी गलत ढंग से अनेक प्रकार से सन्तान के मार्ग यानी सम्भवतः प्रसव-मार्ग में पहुँचा हो, बिगड़ी हुई वायु से पीड़ित और मोहित हो, मूढगर्भ कहते हैं।
english: That fetus (garbha), however, which sometimes has entered the path of the offspring (apatyapatha, probably the birth passage) wrongly and in many ways, afflicted and bewildered by deranged wind (vāyu), they call mūḍhagarbha.
notes: mūḍha = bewildered, stuck; the compound is left as the technical name mūḍhagarbha. 'apatyapatha' = path of the offspring, probably the birth passage (probable). The printed run-together 'garbhaṃkadācidasamyagapatyapathamanekadhā' is read as garbham kadācit asamyak apatya-patham anekadhā. The printed 'pīḍitaṃmohitaṃ' joins two words (spacing). Modern equivalent (probable): mūḍhagarbha = obstructed labour with a malpositioned or stuck fetus (malpresentation); kept as the technical term in the translation.
lines_deva: तं तु गर्भंकदाचिदसम्यगपत्यपथमनेकधा प्रतिपन्नं विगुणेन वायुना पीडितंमोहितं च मूढगर्भमित्याहुः
lines_iast: taṃ tu garbhaṃkadācidasamyagapatyapathamanekadhā pratipannaṃ viguṇena vāyunā pīḍitaṃmohitaṃ ca mūḍhagarbhamityāhuḥ

words.gloss: faulty, deranged; wind (anila); pressing; variety, from

hindi: और, अनुमानित पाठ पर, बिगड़ी वायु के दबाव की विविधता से असंख्य गतियों वाला।
english: And, on a conjectural reading, (one) of countless courses, owing to the variety of the pressing by deranged wind (anila).

text_flags.why: possible: 'asaṃsaṃkhyagātiṃ' has an extra 'saṃ' and a long ā; also 'pratipīḍanaivaicitryāt' has an extra 'ai/i'; the intended reading is probably pratipīḍana-vaicitryāt asaṅkhya-gatim

notes: Elliptical: the verb 'they call' is carried from 87 and not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. GROUPING: appears to continue 87. Printed 'asaṃsaṃkhyagātiṃ' is read as asaṅkhya-gatim with a doubled saṃ and a long ā (print slips, see flag). The sense 'countless courses' agrees with 89 (the courses are then grouped into three). Alternative repair for the middle of the token: pratipīḍanaiva vaicitryāt ('from the variety of the pressing itself'; one 'va' dropped), as plausible as the dropped-'i' repair adopted in words; the sense 'variety of pressing' is the same either way.

hindi: संक्षेप में गति तीन प्रकार की है: ऊर्ध्व, तिरछी और औंधी।
english: In brief, however, the course (gati) is of three kinds: upward, transverse and face-down.

text_flags.why: near certain: 'ūdhrvā' has dh and r transposed; ūrdhvā (upward) fits the list of three courses

notes: Printed 'gatirūdhrvā' is read as gatiḥ ūrdhvā (the dh and r are transposed); printed 'tiryaṅṅyubjā' = tiryaṅ nyubjā. nyubja = face-down, bent over (the exact bodily position is not described here). The copula is understood.

hindi: संस्थान फिर आठ हैं।
english: The positions (saṃsthāna), however, are eight.
notes: Copula understood. saṃsthāna = arrangement, configuration; what is arranged is not stated in this unit; 91 says they will be described later. Printed 'punaraṣṭau' = punaḥ aṣṭau (regular sandhi).

hindi: उन्हें यहीं आगे कहा जाएगा।
english: Those will be told just here, further on.
notes: The printed 'tānyatraivottaratra' = tāni atra eva uttaratra (regular sandhi). The unit does not say what 'those' are; unit 90 (the eight positions) comes just before, and no pairing is asserted.

words.gloss: saṃvaraṇa (closing, covering; the thing closed is not stated)

hindi: उन सब में भी, जिसकी इन्द्रियों के विषय उलटे हो गए हों और जो आक्षेप यानी ऐंठन, योनि के खिसकने, संवरण और मक्कल, जिनका अर्थ यहाँ अस्पष्ट है, श्वास यानी साँस की तकलीफ और भ्रम यानी चक्कर से ग्रस्त हो, तथा जिसका शरीर ठण्डा और जिसकी डकारें दुर्गन्धित हों, उस स्त्री को छोड़ दे।
english: In all of those too, one should avoid the woman whose sense-objects are reversed, who is overtaken by ākṣepa (convulsion), slipping of the yoni, saṃvaraṇa (sense unclear), makkala (sense unclear), breathing trouble and giddiness, whose body is cold, and who has foul belching.
notes: The long compound 'viparītendriyārthām…abhipannām' is taken as one adjective chain for the woman: 'whose sense-objects are reversed' and 'overtaken by' the listed items. saṃvaraṇa and makkala are kept untranslated: saṃvaraṇa means closing or covering (what closes is not said) and makkala is a rare word (in other texts it names a post-delivery pain or clotted blood); neither sense is sure here. 'śvāsa' is rendered 'breathing trouble' as part of a list of troubles; it may also be plain 'breathing'. 'varjayet' = avoid; the unit does not say what is to be avoided in dealing with her (for example the operations of the following units); no object is supplied. The woman's identity (the mūḍhagarbha case) is understood from context.
lines_deva: तेषु सर्वेष्वपि विपरीतेंद्रियार्थामाक्षेपयोनिस्रंशसंवरणमक्कलश्वासभ्रमाभिपन्नां शीतगात्रां पूत्युद्गारां च वर्जयेत्
lines_iast: teṣu sarveṣvapi viparīteṃdriyārthāmākṣepayonisraṃśasaṃvaraṇamakkalaśvāsabhramābhipannāṃ śītagātrāṃ pūtyudgārāṃ ca varjayet

words.gram: m. acc. sg. used as ind.

hindi: पर गर्भशल्य यानी गर्भ के काँटे की क्षण भर भी उपेक्षा न करे।
english: But one should not neglect the garbhaśalya (the fetus as a dart) even for a moment.
notes: garbhaśalya is kept as the technical word: śalya = dart, thorn, or foreign body lodged in the body; 'garbha-śalya' is read as the fetus acting as a śalya. The English 'as a dart' only explains the compound.

hindi: क्योंकि वह शीघ्र ही माता को दम घोंटकर मार देगा।
english: For that, having made (her) breathless, would quickly kill the mother.
notes: The printed 'taddhinirucchvāsīkṛtyāśu' = tat hi nirucchvāsī-kṛtya āśu. 'tat' (neuter) is taken to refer to the garbhaśalya of 93; 'āśu' may belong either to the making breathless or to the killing (it is placed between). The 'her' of 'made her breathless' is not in the Sanskrit and is shown in brackets; the mother is the natural object. Hindi 'दम घोंटकर' renders nirucchvāsī-kṛtya (making breathless).

words.gram: pres. pass. part. vi-√dṝ, m. nom. sg.

hindi: और चेतना वाला गर्भ शस्त्र से चीरा जाता हुआ अंगों को विषम रूप से इधर-उधर फेंके।
english: And a fetus (garbha) that has consciousness, while being split open with a śastra (cutting instrument), may throw its limbs about unevenly.
notes: sacetana = having consciousness, alive; the unit does not say how this is known. 'viṣamam' is taken as an adverb (unevenly, irregularly); it could also be the neuter object 'uneven limbs'. The printed 'sacetanaśca' = sacetanaḥ ca.
lines_deva: सचेतनश्च गर्भः शस्त्रेण विदार्यमाणो विषममंगानि विक्षिपेत्
lines_iast: sacetanaśca garbhaḥ śastreṇa vidāryamāṇo viṣamamaṃgāni vikṣipet

words.gloss: unclear (printed form; on a conjectural reading 'for delivery')

hindi: इसलिए उसके अटकने पर अनुमानित पाठ पर प्रसव के लिए प्रयत्न करें, और पहले कहे हुए मन्त्र और औषध प्रयोग में लाए।
english: Therefore, in the obstruction (saṅga) of that, on a conjectural reading, they should strive for delivery, and one should apply the earlier-stated mantras and medicines (auṣadha).

text_flags.why: possible: 'sūtyaḥ' (visarga) does not fit; the dative sūtyai ('for delivery') suits 'prayateran'

notes: The printed 'sūtyaḥ' does not fit the grammar (a plural nominative 'sūtayaḥ' is not needed); 'sūtyai' (dative, 'for delivery') is conjectured, with the subject of 'prayateran' (they) not stated. 'tatsaṅge' = in the obstruction of that; the referent of 'that' (the fetus or its sticking) is not stated, and saṅga is taken up in 97. The shift from plural 'prayateran' to singular 'prayuñjīta' is noted. 'pūrvoktāni' is taken with both mantras and medicines; the earlier passage it points to is not named here.
lines_deva: तस्मात्तत्संगे सूत्यः प्रयतेरन् पूर्वोक्तानि च मंत्रौषधानि प्रयुंजीत
lines_iast: tasmāttatsaṃge sūtyaḥ prayateran pūrvoktāni ca maṃtrauṣadhāni prayuṃjīta

hindi: सङ्ग तीन प्रकार का होता है।
english: The obstruction (saṅga), however, is of three kinds.
notes: Printed 'trividhastu' = trividhaḥ tu. saṅga = sticking, obstruction (of the fetus, understood from 96).

hindi: सिर में, कन्धे में, या जघन यानी कूल्हे के भाग में।
english: In the head, in the shoulder, or in the jaghana (hip region).
notes: Elliptical: no verb; GROUPING: appears to continue 97 (the three kinds of saṅga). jaghana = hip region (loins, buttocks); the exact part is not defined here. Printed 'śirasyaṃse' = śirasi aṃse (regular sandhi). Whether the three are 'the three kinds' is not stated. Obstetric reading (probable, not stated by the text): the three kinds of saṅga correspond to head, shoulder and breech (buttock) obstruction; 'jaghana' here = hip/buttock region.

words.gloss: afterbirth (jarāyu); causing to fall; commonness, same

hindi: मूढगर्भ में तो जरायु यानी जेर को गिराने के समान कर्म है, ऐसा कुछ लोग कहते हैं।
english: For a mūḍhagarbha, however, the procedure (karma) is the same as the causing of the jarāyu (afterbirth) to fall, some say.
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'say' (āhuḥ) is not stated; 'some say' is the sense of 'iti eke'. jarāyu = afterbirth, placenta/membranes (standard); the earlier glossary uses aparā for placenta. 'sāmānya' is rendered 'the same as', its plain sense is 'common to'. This is one opinion of three given in 99-101; the text does not say which is held.

hindi: मन्त्र आदि का कर्म अथर्ववेद में बताया गया है, ऐसा कुछ लोग कहते हैं।
english: Some say that the procedure beginning with mantras is prescribed in the Atharvaveda.

text_flags.why: near certain: 'karmārtharva' has an extra r; karma + atharva = karmātharva (the Atharvaveda)

notes: Printed 'karmārtharvaveda…' has an extra r (karma + atharva gives karmātharva), see flag. 'Atharvaveda-vihita' is taken as 'prescribed in/by the Atharvaveda'. 'ādi' = beginning with; the other steps are not listed. The printed 'maṃtrādikarmārtharvavedavihitam' is one token.

hindi: देखे हुए कर्म वाले, शल्य निकालने वाले के द्वारा शल्य यानी काँटे या भीतर फँसी वस्तु का निकालना है, ऐसा कुछ लोग कहते हैं।
english: Some say: the extraction of the śalya (dart, foreign body) is by a śalya-remover (śalyahartṛ) whose work has been seen (dṛṣṭakarman).
notes: Copula understood. 'dṛṣṭakarman' = one whose work has been seen (an experienced practitioner); not enriched. 'śalyahartṛ' = remover of the śalya (a surgeon, probable); the fetus is the śalya in this context (see 93), not stated here. 'iti eke' = some (say).

hindi: वास्तव में शस्त्रकर्म यानी शस्त्र से किया जाने वाला कर्म सबसे कठिन है।
english: In truth, śastrakarma (work with the cutting instrument, surgery) is the most difficult.
notes: kaṣṭatama is rendered 'most difficult' (kaṣṭa = hard, painful, troublesome); 'most painful' is also possible. The modern word 'surgery' stands beside the Sanskrit term only to name it.

words.gloss: yoni; liver (yakṛt); spleen (plīha); intestines (antra); womb (garbhāśaya; standard); and the like

words.gram: pres. part. an-upa-√hiṃs, m. inst. sg.
pres. part. caus. a-√spṛś, m. inst. sg.

words.gloss: to be fixed, held in view; possibly 'avacāryam', to be applied

hindi: क्योंकि योनि, यकृत्, प्लीहा, आँतों, गर्भाशय आदि के बीच, उन्हें चोट न पहुँचाने वाले और न छुआने वाले के द्वारा शस्त्र निश्चित किया जाना चाहिए; और खींचकर ऊपर करना, नीचे खींचना, घुमाना, काटकर निकालना, काटना, चीरना, दबाना और सीधा करना एक हाथ से करने चाहिए।
english: Since, among the yoni, liver, spleen, intestines, womb (garbhāśaya) and the like, the instrument has to be fixed (avadhārya) by one who does not injure them and does not cause touching; and pulling up, pulling down, turning round, cutting out, cutting through, splitting, pressing and straightening are to be done with one hand.

text_flags.why: possible: 'avadhāryam' may be a misprint of 'avacāryam' (to be applied), cf. avacārayet in 112; dh/c confusion is plausible in this print

notes: Hard unit; confidence is medium to low. 'avadhāryam' (to be fixed, held in view) is printed; 'avacāryam' (to be applied; cf. avacārayet in 112) is a possible original, see flag. 'tān anupahiṃsatā asparśayatā' is read as 'by one who neither injures them nor lets (it, the instrument) touch (them)'; the object of 'asparśayatā' is not stated, so this is a reading. 'madhye' with the list: 'among'. The printed forms 'vyāvarttana', 'utkarttana' show the book-wide rtt spelling (normalised to rt); 'pīḍanarjūkaraṇāni' = pīḍana-ṛjūkaraṇāni (a+ṛ gives ar). The eight operations are listed as neuter nouns with 'kāryāṇi'; 'ekena pāṇinā' = with one hand. Continues from 102 (the reason: GROUPING appears to continue 102).
lines_deva: यतो योनियकृत्प्लीहान्त्रगर्भाशयादीनां मध्ये ताननुपहिंसताऽस्पर्शयता शस्त्रमवधार्यमुत्कर्षणापकर्षणव्यावर्त्तनोत्कर्त्तनच्छेदनभेदनपीडनर्जूकरणानि चैकेन पाणिना कार्याणि
lines_iast: yato yoniyakṛtplīhāntragarbhāśayādīnāṃ madhye tānanupahiṃsatā'sparśayatā śastramavadhāryamutkarṣaṇāpakarṣaṇavyāvarttanotkarttanacchedanabhedanapīḍanarjūkaraṇāni caikena pāṇinā kāryāṇi

words.gram: m. acc. sg. used as adj.

hindi: इसलिए ईश्वर यानी स्वामी से पूछकर और परम प्रयत्न का सहारा लेकर, उसे जानने वालों के साथ उसका उपक्रम करे।
english: Therefore, having consulted the īśvara (lord), and having resorted to supreme effort, accompanied by those who know it, one should undertake it.
notes: īśvara = lord, master (here probably a ruler or head of the household; not defined, so left as 'lord'); not the divine. 'tadvidya' is taken as those who know that (the craft). 'tam' (masculine) is rendered 'it'; the referent is not named (the case or the fetus; unclear). 'paraṃ' is taken with 'yatnam' (supreme effort); the printed 'yatnamāsthāyatadvidyasahitastamupakramet' runs words together, split here without a flag.

words.gloss: in non-action, if no action is taken

hindi: कर्म न करने पर मृत्यु निश्चित है।
english: In inaction, death is certain.
notes: Copula understood. The subject (mother or the woman) is not stated.

words.gloss: udara (a disease of the belly, probably ascites-type); aśmarī (urinary stone; standard); and so on

hindi: वैसे ही उदर यानी पेट के रोग, सम्भवतः जलोदर की प्रकृति के, अश्मरी यानी पथरी आदि का भी।
english: Likewise also of udara (a belly disease, probably ascites-type), aśmarī (urinary stone) and so on.

text_flags.why: possible: the genitive plural 'prabhṛtīnām' has lost its anusvara before api

notes: Elliptical: no verb; what is said of them (that surgery is needed, or that death follows inaction) is not stated and is not supplied. Printed 'prabhṛtīnāpi' lacks the anusvara of prabhṛtīnām (see flag). udara here is the disease (belly disease, probably ascites-type: probable) beside aśmarī; elsewhere in the book it can mean the belly. GROUPING: appears to continue 105.

words.gloss: cloth; pad (cumbhala); raised; hip, waist; region
śālmalī (silk-cotton tree, Bombax ceiba; standard); picchā (gum, slime; probable)

hindi: फिर उत्तान यानी चित लेटी हुई, मुड़ी जाँघों वाली और वस्त्र के चुम्भल यानी सम्भवतः गद्दी से उठाए गए कटि-प्रदेश वाली स्त्री के लिए, धन्वनागमृत्तिका, जिसका अर्थ अस्पष्ट है, शाल्मली-पिच्छा यानी सम्भवतः सेमल के गोंद और घी से हाथ और योनि को चुपड़कर गर्भ को निकाले।
english: Then, in the case of her who lies face up, with the thighs bent and the hip region raised by a cloth cumbhala (probably a pad), having anointed the hand and the yoni with dhanvanāgamṛttikā (unclear), śālmalī-picchā (probably the gum of the silk-cotton tree, Bombax ceiba) and ghee (ghṛta), one should extract the fetus (garbha).
notes: dhanvanāgamṛttikā is kept as printed and unsplit: it may hide mṛttikā (clay, earth) with a preceding word, but the division is not safe, so it is left unclear. śālmalī = silk-cotton tree, Bombax ceiba (standard); picchā in 'śālmalī-picchā' = its gum (probable), as elsewhere in the book. 'cumbhala' (printed cuṃbhala) is taken as a pad or roll (probably a variant of cumbala/cumbaka; probable). Genitives 'uttānāyāḥ…' stand loosely ('in the case of'). The printed 'athottānāyā' etc. are regular sandhi. The anointing is of the hand and the yoni (the objects of abhyajya).
lines_deva: अथोत्तानाया व्याभुग्नसक्थ्या वस्त्रचुंभलोन्नमितकटिप्रदेशायाश्च धन्वनागमृत्तिकाशाल्मलीपिच्छाघृतैरभ्यज्य हस्तं योनिंच गर्भमाहरेत्
lines_iast: athottānāyā vyābhugnasakthyā vastracuṃbhalonnamitakaṭipradeśāyāśca dhanvanāgamṛttikāśālmalīpicchāghṛtairabhyajya hastaṃ yoniṃca garbhamāharet

words.gloss: because of following the natural direction (ānulomya)

hindi: वहाँ दोनों जाँघों से आए हुए का, आनुलोम्य यानी स्वाभाविक दिशा में होने के कारण, केवल कटा हुआ।
english: There, of one who has come by the two thighs, because of ānulomya (following the natural direction), only cut (chinna).
notes: The sense is uncertain and the unit is elliptical (no verb or noun for what is cut or to be cut is given and none is supplied); 'chinnam eva' may mean that only cutting is done, or may be a corrupt reading (an alternative such as 'achinnam' is not adopted). 'sakthibhyām āgata' is taken as presenting by the two thighs; the printed run-together 'sakthibhyāmāgatasyānulomyācchinnameva' is split without a flag (regular sandhi). Not enriched.

words.gloss: of the one who has entered, presented

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, n. acc. sg. used as ind.

words.gloss: of the one who has entered, presented

hindi: जिसकी एक जाँघ आगे आई हो उसकी दूसरी जाँघ को फैलाकर; जो नितम्ब-प्रदेश से आया हो उसके नितम्ब-प्रदेश को दबाकर ऊपर उठाकर और दोनों जाँघों को फैलाकर; जो तिरछा आया हो घुमाकर, या पिछले आधे भाग को उठाकर अगले आधे भाग को सीधा करके सन्तान के मार्ग में लाकर; जिसका सिर बगल की ओर घूमा हो उसके कन्धे को दबाकर ऊपर उठाकर सिर को सन्तान के मार्ग में लाकर; जिसकी दोनों भुजाएँ आगे आई हों उसके दोनों कन्धों को ऊपर की ओर दबाकर सिर की जड़ को लाकर निकाले।
english: For one who has presented with one thigh, having stretched out the other thigh; for one who has come at the buttock region, having pressed down the buttock region and lifted upward, having stretched out the two thighs; for one who has come transversely, having turned round, or having lifted the hind half and brought the front half to the path of the offspring straight; for one whose head is turned to the side, having pressed the shoulder and lifted upward, having brought the head to the path of the offspring; for one who has presented both arms, having pressed the two shoulders upward and brought the base of the head, one should draw out.

text_flags.why: possible: the dual of sakthi (neuter) is sakthinī; 'sakthyanī' has an extra y
possible: the absolutive is prasārya; the final e looks like a print slip
possible: 'parādarddham' has an extra da; aparārdha (hind half) is intended, in contrast to pūrvārdha (front half)

notes: One sentence with a series of cases; the one verb 'nirharet' (should draw out) closes it, and no object is stated. Each case begins with a genitive 'for one who…'; the 'one' is the fetus by context only. 'apatyapatha' = path of the offspring, probably the birth passage (probable). 'pratyārjavam' is taken as 'toward straightness' and may be a different word; the sense 'straight' is plain. In 'śirasoṃ'saṃ' and 'utpīḍyāṃ'sau' the printed apostrophe is a print habit before aṃsa; no flag. The rdd spelling in 'parādarddham/pūrvārddham' is the book-wide normalisation to rd. 'sphigdeśa' is the buttock region (sphik/sphij). The sense of the lifting is as printed ('ūrdhvam utkṣipya'); the text does not say what is lifted beyond the object named. Modern equivalents (probable, not stated by the text): the cases look like one leg presenting, breech (sphik-deśa), transverse lie (tiryak), head turned aside, and both arms presenting.
lines_deva: एकस्मिन् सक्थ्नि प्रपन्नस्येतरं सक्थि प्रसार्य स्फिग्देशागतस्य स्फिग्देशंप्रनिपीड्योर्ध्वमुत्क्षिप्य सक्थ्यनी प्रसार्ये तिर्यगागतस्य परिवर्त्य वाऽपरादर्द्धमुत्क्षिप्य पूर्वार्द्धमपत्यपथं प्रत्यार्जवमानीय पार्श्ववृत्तशिरसोंऽसं प्रतिपीड्योर्ध्वमुत्क्षिप्य शिरोऽपत्यपथमानीय बाहुद्वयं प्रपन्नस्योर्ध्वमुत्पीड्यांऽसौ शिरोमूलमानीय निर्हरेत्
lines_iast: ekasmin sakthni prapannasyetaraṃ sakthi prasārya sphigdeśāgatasya sphigdeśaṃpranipīḍyordhvamutkṣipya sakthyanī prasārye tiryagāgatasya parivartya vā'parādarddhamutkṣipya pūrvārddhamapatyapathaṃ pratyārjavamānīya pārśvavṛttaśirasoṃ'saṃ pratipīḍyordhvamutkṣipya śiro'patyapathamānīya bāhudvayaṃ prapannasyordhvamutpīḍyāṃ'sau śiromūlamānīya nirharet

hindi: पर जो मुड़े हुए मध्य भाग वाला हाथ, पैर और सिर से योनि में आता है।
english: But the one who, with its middle bent, comes to the yoni with hands, feet and head.

text_flags.why: possible: 'abhyugna' is not a known word; abhugna (bent) is used in the next unit

notes: The relative clause is complete; its main clause is in 112 ('tau mūḍhau'), so the sentence continues over 110-112 (GROUPING: appears to continue into 111 and 112). 'pratipadyate' = enters/reaches; rendered 'comes to'. Printed 'abhyugna' is not a word; see flag (cf. abhugna in 111).

hindi: और जो मुड़ा हुआ ही एक पैर से योनि में और दूसरे से गुदा में।
english: And the one who, just bent, (comes) with one foot to the yoni, with the second to the anus (pāyu).
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'pratipadyate' is carried from 110 and is not supplied. pāyu = anus (standard). The printed 'yaścābhugnaevaikena' = yaḥ ca abhugnaḥ eva ekena (regular sandhi, hiatus). GROUPING: appears to continue 110.

hindi: वे दोनों मूढ़ हाथ से निकाले नहीं जा सकते, इसलिए शस्त्र का प्रयोग करे।
english: Those two, mūḍha, cannot be extracted by the hand; thus one should apply the instrument (śastra).
notes: 'iti' closes the reason ('thinking: they cannot be extracted by hand'); rendered with 'thus' and left out of any quotation. 'aśakyau' = not possible (to be) (inf. in passive sense). 'tau' = the two cases of 110 and 111; the text does not say so in so many words. Hindi 'मूढ़' keeps the technical sense (stuck); not enriched.

words.gloss: round; tip (maṇḍalāgra, a round-tipped knife; probable)

hindi: फिर स्त्री को आश्वस्त करके, मण्डलाग्र यानी सम्भवतः गोल नोक वाले शस्त्र या अंगुलिशस्त्र यानी सम्भवतः उँगली के शस्त्र से चीरकर, सिर की खोपड़ी के टुकड़े निकालकर, शंकु से ठोड़ी, तालु, छाती या काँख में पकड़कर हटा ले।
english: Then, having comforted the woman, having split open with a maṇḍalāgra (probably a round-tipped knife) or an aṅguliśastra (probably a finger-knife), having removed the pieces of the skull, having seized with a hook (śaṅku) at the chin, the palate, the chest or the armpit, one should draw (it) away.

text_flags.why: possible: 'tāluki' is not a form (tālu is neuter, loc. tāluni); ni misread as ki

notes: The objects of 'vidārya' and 'apaharet' are not stated (the head or the fetus by context); '(it)' is shown in brackets. 'tāluni urasi' replaces the printed 'tālukyurasi' (see flag). Whether the hook seizes at the chin, palate, chest or armpit, or the fetus is drawn from them, is not settled by the wording; the first is the plainer reading. maṇḍalāgra and aṅguliśastra are instrument names; the tags are probable. Printed 'athastriyamāśvāsya' joins atha and striyam (spacing).
lines_deva: अथस्त्रियमाश्वास्य मंडलाग्रेणांगुलिशस्त्रेण वा विदार्य शिरःकपालान्याहृत्य शंकुना गृहीत्वा चुबुके तालुक्युरसि कक्षायां वाऽपहरेत्
lines_iast: athastriyamāśvāsya maṃḍalāgreṇāṃguliśastreṇa vā vidārya śiraḥkapālānyāhṛtya śaṃkunā gṛhītvā cubuke tālukyurasi kakṣāyāṃ vā'paharet

words.gloss: eye; projection, rim (akṣikūṭa; probably the eye-socket rim; probable)

hindi: या जिसका सिर विदीर्ण न हुआ हो, अक्षिकूट यानी सम्भवतः आँख के गड्ढे के किनारे पर या गण्ड यानी गाल में।
english: Or one whose head is unsplit, at the akṣikūṭa (the eye-socket rim, probably) or at the cheek (gaṇḍa).
notes: Elliptical: no verb; the action (seizing with the hook, drawing away) is carried from 113 and not supplied. GROUPING: appears to continue 113. The unstated noun after 'abhinnaśirasam' is the fetus by context. akṣikūṭa = projection or rim of the eye region; the exact part is not firm. gaṇḍa = cheek (it can also mean temple).

hindi: वैसे ही कन्धे में अटके हुए का कन्धे के स्थान पर भुजा को काटकर; दृति यानी चमड़े की मशक की तरह फूले हुए का वायु से भरे पेट को चीरकर और आँतों को निकालकर, ढीले हुए को निकाले।
english: Likewise, for one stuck at the shoulder, having cut off the arm at the shoulder region; for one swollen like a skin-bag (dṛti), having split open the belly (udara) full of wind (vāta) and cast out the intestines, one should extract (it) when it has become slack.
notes: The objects of 'chittvā' etc. and of 'āharet' are not stated; '(it)' is shown in brackets. 'dṛteḥ iva ādhmātasya': dṛti = a skin or leather bag (a bellows or water-skin); the ablative is read as the case of comparison used loosely ('like'). 'vāta-pūrṇam' = full of wind (vāta, plain wind). The printed spelling 'chitvā' (single t) is a spelling variant of chittvā, recorded here once for the chunk (also in 119); no flag. Printed 'tathā'ṃsa…' shows the print habit of an avagraha before aṃsa.
lines_deva: तथाऽंससंसक्तस्यांसदेशे बाहुं छित्वा दृतेरिवाध्मातस्य वातपूर्णमुदरमवदार्य निरस्यांत्राणि शिथिलीभूतमाहरेत्
lines_iast: tathā'ṃsasaṃsaktasyāṃsadeśe bāhuṃ chitvā dṛterivādhmātasya vātapūrṇamudaramavadārya nirasyāṃtrāṇi śithilībhūtamāharet

hindi: जघन में अटके हुए का जघन की हड्डियों को तोड़कर।
english: For one stuck at the hips (jaghana), having broken the hip bones (jaghana-kapāla).

text_flags.why: possible: 'śakta' (able) does not fit; sakta (stuck) matches aṃsa-saṃsakta in 115

notes: Elliptical: the verb 'should extract' is carried from 115 and not supplied. kapāla = plate or bone (as in the skull-pieces of 113); jaghana-kapāla = the bones of the hip region (probably the pelvic bones; probable). The closing 'iti' ends the list of cases (kept out of the translation). Printed 'śakta' is read as 'sakta' (stuck), see flag. GROUPING: appears to continue 115.

hindi: और इस विषय में ये हैं।
english: And on this there are (verses).
notes: A formula introducing the verses that follow. 'verses' is the usual understood noun and is shown in brackets; it is not in the Sanskrit. The printed 'cātra' = ca atra.

hindi: गर्भ का जो-जो अंग वायु के वश अटक जाए, खण्ड-खण्ड।
english: Whatever limb of the fetus (garbha) may get stuck by the power of wind (vāyu), piecemeal.
notes: 'khaṇḍaśaḥ' (in pieces) most likely belongs with the cutting in 119 ('having cut it piece by piece'); here it is given at the end as printed. The relative clause is completed by 119 (GROUPING: appears to continue into 119). Printed 'yadyadvāyuvaśādaṃgaṃ' = yat yat vāyu-vaśāt aṅgam; 'vāyu' is plain wind here.

hindi: उस-उस को काटकर भली प्रकार निकाले, और माता को चोट से बचाए।
english: Having cut that and that, one should remove it properly, and protect the mother from injury.
notes: Printed 'tattacchitvā' = tat tat chittvā (chitvā spelling variant, see 115). The printed 'haretsamyagrakṣejjananīṃ' = haret samyak rakṣet jananīm. 'tat tat' repeats the relative 'yat yat' of 118 ('each such'). Continues 118.

words.gram: pres. part. a-√pat, f. acc. sg.

hindi: फिर न गिरती हुई अपरा यानी जेर को वैद्य पहले की तरह गिराए।
english: Then the physician should cause the aparā (placenta) that is not falling to fall, as before.
notes: aparā = placenta, afterbirth (standard). 'as before' (pūrvavat) points to an earlier procedure, probably the one for the afterbirth in 99 or earlier units; the unit does not say which. Printed 'athāpataṃtīmaparāṃ' = atha apatantīm aparām (regular sandhi).
